Class MKFocus

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.MKFocus
public final class MKFocus extends Object
MK-managed focus registration + screen-level focus utilities.

Why this exists

MenuKit's panel system intercepts clicks within panel bounds (the opacity contract). That interception SUPPRESSES vanilla's natural focus-transition mechanism, which only fires when a vanilla widget actively claims a click via Screen.children() iteration. On empty-space clicks (in-panel OR outside-panel), no widget claims, so vanilla never calls Screen.setFocused(...) — a previously- focused widget stays focused indefinitely and silently swallows subsequent keystrokes.

Two complementary fixes restore expected UX:

  1. In-panel empty-space clicks — the opacity-eat code paths (in VanillaScreenPanelAdapter and ScreenPanelRegistry) call screen.setFocused(null) before returning the eat.
  2. Outside-panel clicks — handled by an init()-installed Fabric ScreenMouseEvents.afterMouseClick listener. After vanilla's dispatch runs, if the focused widget is MK-managed (registered via addWidget(Screen, T)) AND the click was outside its bounds, the listener clears focus. Scoping to MK-managed widgets avoids changing vanilla's behavior for non-MK widgets on the same screen.

The outside-panel path uses a Fabric API event rather than a mixin because Screen doesn't override mouseClicked in 26.2 — it inherits the default method from ContainerEventHandler, so there's no bytecode in Screen.class for a mixin to inject into. The Fabric event is the upstream-approved injection point.

Consumer contract

Consumer mods that register focusable widgets via MK (TextField, Keybindery's SearchBox, future MK-adjacent input widgets) call addWidget(Screen, T) instead of ScreenAccessor.mk$addWidget directly. This wraps the underlying registration AND opts the widget into MK-managed focus semantics. Pair with removeWidget(Screen, GuiEventListener) on teardown.

clear(Screen) is the canonical "blur whatever is focused right now" helper — usable as defense-in-depth before triggering input modes that should start from a clean focus state (chord capture, modal confirms, navigation handoffs).

Lifecycle

Tracking is keyed by Screen reference via WeakHashMap, so screen GC naturally evicts entries. Widget references inside the per-screen set are strong — widget lifetime is dominated by the screen's own children-list ownership, so the strong reference doesn't extend lifetime beyond what vanilla already does.

  • Method Details

    • init

      public static void init()
      Registers the global ScreenEvents.AFTER_INIT listener that wires ScreenMouseEvents.afterMouseClick on every opened screen for outside-bounds focus janitor. Called once from MKClient.onInitializeClient.

      The per-screen listeners are GC'd naturally when the screen instance is collected; no explicit teardown.

    • blurOnOutsideBounds

      public static void blurOnOutsideBounds(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen, double mouseX, double mouseY)
      Core focus-janitor rule, shared by the afterMouseClick listener AND the MK panel-adapter in-panel dispatch sites.

      If a focused MK-managed widget exists AND the click landed OUTSIDE its bounds, clear focus on the screen. Inside-bounds clicks leave focus alone — letting either vanilla's natural setFocused-on-claim flow handle the transition, or the widget legitimately retain focus on a no-op interaction (e.g., clicking the already-focused TextField again).

      Scope: only MK-managed widgets (registered via addWidget(Screen, T)). Non-MK focused widgets keep vanilla focus semantics — no behavioral change for non-MK consumers sharing a screen with MK panels.

      Called from:

      • onAfterMouseClick(Screen, MouseButtonEvent, boolean) — after vanilla's Screen.mouseClicked (out-of-panel clicks)
      • VanillaScreenPanelAdapter.mouseClicked — after any in-panel dispatch path (overlay match, element claim, or opacity-eat fallthrough)
      • ScreenPanelRegistry.dispatchCoveredClick — after the opaque-at-cursor dispatch for container screens
      The unified rule means clicking any MK button, dropdown, etc. that doesn't itself take focus blurs a focused MK text input — matching vanilla's "claimant gets focus, others lose it" behavior for non-focus-taking MK elements.

    • addWidget

      public static <T extends net.minecraft.client.gui.components.events.GuiEventListener & net.minecraft.client.gui.narration.NarratableEntry> T addWidget(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen, T widget)
      Registers a widget with the given screen for input dispatch AND MK-managed focus semantics. Wraps ScreenAccessor.mk$addWidget(T) — the widget is added to the screen's children + narratables lists (so vanilla's input pipeline dispatches to it) and recorded in MK's focus-tracking set (so MKFocusJanitorMixin clears its focus on outside-bounds clicks).

      Returns the widget for fluent-style chaining (matching vanilla's addWidget return signature).

    • removeWidget

      public static void removeWidget(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen, net.minecraft.client.gui.components.events.GuiEventListener widget)
      Symmetric counterpart to addWidget(Screen, T). Removes the widget from the screen's input pipeline AND from MK's focus-tracking set. Safe to call even if the widget was never registered (no-op).

    • clear

      public static void clear(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen)
      Clears focus from any widget currently focused on the given screen. Convenience pass-through to screen.setFocused(null) — exposed at MK's API surface for discoverability and to give consumers a defense-in-depth path (e.g., before triggering a chord-capture flow or other input mode that should start from a clean focus state).

      The opacity-eat code paths and the focus-janitor mixin also clear focus automatically in their respective scenarios — this method is for consumer-driven clears outside those flows.

    • isManaged

      public static boolean isManaged(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen, net.minecraft.client.gui.components.events.GuiEventListener widget)
      Tests whether a widget is MK-managed on the given screen. Used by the afterMouseClick listener and the widget-hover-suppression mixin to scope their behavior to MK-registered widgets (the suppressor SKIPS suppression for MK-managed widgets so MK-placed widgets like TextField's wrapped EditBox keep their hover / cursor feedback even when "underneath" the panel they belong to).

    • isCursorCovered

      public static boolean isCursorCovered(double mouseX, double mouseY)
      Post-Phase 18r-5: is the cursor currently covered by any visible MK content on the active screen? A point is covered when some panel claims it via the unified ScreenPanelRegistry.panelClaimsPoint(Panel, ScreenOrigin, int, double, double) test — an opaque background (minus per-element holes), an active overlay (e.g., an open Dropdown popover extending beyond its owning panel), or a solid interactive element. Combines queries across ScreenPanelRegistry (container-screen + lambda-active adapters) AND VanillaScreenPanelRegistry (non-container vanilla-screen adapters) — one claim definition for all.

      Used by the widget-hover-suppression mixin to stop vanilla buttons / list rows from rendering hover highlights when the cursor is "over" them but visually covered by MK content. The opacity-eat input path routes the click away; this closes the visual loop.

    • isCursorCoveredAtCursor

      public static boolean isCursorCoveredAtCursor()
      No-arg variant of isCursorCovered(double, double) for callers without mouse coords as parameters (e.g., the tooltip-suppression mixin which fires inside GuiGraphicsExtractor.setTooltipForNextFrame). Reads cursor position from MouseHandler and converts to GUI-scaled coords using the same formula as MKModalMouseHandlerMixin.

    • isInertUnderPanel

      public static boolean isInertUnderPanel(double mouseX, double mouseY)
      THE unified inertness predicate — the single source of truth every suppression site consults so they cannot disagree about whether vanilla content at a screen point is covered by MenuKit content. A point is inert iff vanilla there should receive nothing: no click / release / scroll, no hover, no highlight, no tooltip.

      Inert iff EITHER:

      • a visible modal-tracking panel exists — a modal claims the WHOLE screen, so everything behind it is inert; OR
      • some panel covers (mouseX, mouseY) — its opaque background (minus per-element click-through holes), an active overlay, OR a solid interactive element — across container, lambda, AND vanilla- screen adapters, all through the one ScreenPanelRegistry.panelClaimsPoint(Panel, ScreenOrigin, int, double, double) test (see isCursorCovered(double, double)).

      Every hover / highlight / tooltip suppressor and the press/release/ scroll eat all reduce to this one question, so a new vanilla surface (a creative tab, a new widget kind) can't fall through a per-site predicate gap. The input path's dispatch-returning twin (it also returns the panel to route the input to) is ScreenPanelRegistry.findCoveringPanelAt(Screen, double, double).

    • isInertUnderPanelAtCursor

      public static boolean isInertUnderPanelAtCursor()
      No-coord variant of isInertUnderPanel(double, double) — reads the cursor position from MouseHandler (for suppressors that fire without coords, e.g. the tooltip and list-hover mixins).
